# Install Safety and Recovery Checklist: PB Store on the Reader

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for interrupted operations, power loss, battery and free-space checks, a dropping Wi-Fi, leaving the store, recovery of operations left by the installer or the store, and the self-update (staging, swap at next start, fallback) are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before planning.
**Created**: 2026-10-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: requirements only (spec.md, constitution 2.1.0 Principles IV, V, VI and VII, and the contracts of feature 002 that the spec relies on: journal, reader-layout, install-record). Depth: formal pre-plan gate. Audience: author and reviewer. There is no plan.md yet, so items that need a design decision are marked `[Gap]` and should be settled in the plan or by editing the spec. Items that repeat the installer's own safety checklist (`specs/002-pb-installer-linux/checklists/install-safety.md`) are left out; this list asks only what is new on the reader.

## Interrupted Operations and Power Loss

- [x] CHK001 Is it stated which operation kinds the "old or new complete version" guarantee covers on the reader (install, update, remove, adopt, repair, self-update, deletion of a data folder), including that deleting a data folder has no journal and may end partly done? [Completeness, Spec §FR-029, §FR-036, §SC-003]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Assumptions (what the guarantee covers; data-folder deletion has no journal, E-INS-33/37), FR-029, SC-003.
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec say whether the guarantee holds when power is lost *while the reader's own desktop is running and may itself read or rewrite `view.json`*, or is this left to the unverified device facts? [Gap, Assumption, Spec §Background device facts, §FR-040]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Assumptions (desktop may rewrite view.json; E-INS-25; DS-05), Background table.
- [x] CHK003 Is the "commit point" named in the store's requirements (not only in the installer's journal contract), so that "finish" versus "undo" in the messages, in the home-key rule and in the cancel rule all mean the same instant? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §FR-025, §FR-028]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-017 (commit point = the engine's `30-commit` marker; used by FR-025 and the Cancel rule).
- [x] CHK004 Is the note that lets the next start say "cancelled, nothing changed" stored somewhere that survives a power loss, and is it listed among the entities and the writes the store may make? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases "home key", §Key Entities, §FR-040]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Key Entities (Pending note), FR-025, FR-040; data-model PendingNote; store-state-folder.
- [x] CHK005 Are the rule ids and the three-part message defined for the outcomes of a *repair* (finished, undone, could not finish), not only for failures of a new action? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, §FR-028]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-028 (finished / undone / E-INS-24), contracts/ui-pages.md Result wording, FR-019.
- [x] CHK006 Is the state between two apps in "Update all" defined after an interruption (no queue is kept; the next start shows what is left), so that no app is left updated or half-updated without a message? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-021 (each app its own journaled operation, no queue, remaining apps still show update available).
- [x] CHK007 Is it stated what a user sees, and what is blocked, while a repair is pending and the app being repaired is one the user wants to open from the reader's menu? [Gap, Spec §FR-028; compare installer FR-018 "may be unusable"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-028 and ui-pages Repair page (the app may be unusable until repaired; the reader's menu cannot be blocked).

## Battery and Free-Space Checks

- [x] CHK008 Is the minimum battery charge quantified in the spec or by a stated rule for choosing it, instead of "fixed in the plan"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016, §Edge Cases "battery is low"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-016 states the numbers (25 % / 10 %), research R-07.
- [x] CHK009 Is the behavior defined when the reader is on a charger or a USB cable (does the level still count), and when the battery level cannot be read? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-016]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-016, research R-07 (charging 10 %, unreadable level needs an explicit tap, E-STO-05).
- [x] CHK010 Is it specified what happens when the charge falls below the minimum *during* an operation (after the first write): continue, undo, or finish first? [Gap, Spec §FR-016]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-016 (a falling level during an operation changes nothing), research R-07.
- [x] CHK011 Does the battery rule for a repair avoid a dead end (a pending repair that cannot start because the battery is low, while other actions are blocked until the repair is done) and say what the user is told? [Conflict, Spec §FR-016 vs §FR-028]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-016 (repair minimum 10 %; below it the repair waits, browsing works, message says to charge).
- [x] CHK012 Is the battery and space check required before the launcher swaps a prepared self-update at the next start, and what happens to the update if either check fails (stay prepared, be dropped, message by whom)? [Gap, Spec §FR-033]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-033 (space check for the swap, no battery check and why, the update stays staged and is retried), launcher contract W1.
- [x] CHK013 Is the point in the flow at which free space is checked consistent with the download: the spec runs the checks after the download (§FR-015), so is a catalog-based check of needed against free space required *before* downloading up to 64 MiB over Wi-Fi? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015, §Edge Cases "Not enough free storage"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-015 (refuse before downloading when free < package_size + 10 MiB), research R-08.
- [x] CHK014 Does "space needed" count the downloaded package kept in the store's own area in addition to staging and the new files, and is the space rule of feature 002 (cluster rounding, 10 MiB margin) restated or referenced for the reader? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, §Assumptions "package up to 64 MiB"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-015 (space rule of feature 002 restated; the package is in memory, so it adds no storage).
- [x] CHK015 For a self-update, does the space rule count the old version, the new version and the prepared copy at the same time, since the old version is kept until the new one has started once? [Gap, Spec §FR-032, §FR-034]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-033 (room for one more program copy: run, previous and staged exist at once), research R-08.
- [x] CHK016 Is the edge case "free memory of the reader does not allow it" separated from storage space, or are memory and storage conflated in one sentence and one rule id? [Ambiguity, Spec §Edge Cases "package is larger than 64 MiB"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-015 and Edge Cases (E-INS-07 storage and E-STO-03 memory are separate).

## Wi-Fi and Downloads

- [x] CHK017 Is it stated whether an interrupted download is ever resumed or always started again from the beginning, and is that consistent with deleting the partial file? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases "download stops", §FR-015]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-006 and Edge Cases (a download is never resumed).
- [x] CHK018 Is the cleanup of a partial or finished download defined for the case where the app was ended (battery, home key, crash) before it could delete it, including who deletes it and when? [Gap, Spec §FR-015, §FR-025]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-015 (no download file exists on the reader, so nothing to clean up), research R-02.
- [x] CHK019 Is "no progress for 30 seconds" defined for each network step (connect, catalog, package) and for a connection that is up but very slow, so the rule can be checked? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-006 (steps named: connect, catalog, package; slow-but-progressing is not no-progress), research R-06.
- [x] CHK020 Is the Wi-Fi state after a *dropped* connection specified (the store switched it on, the connection fails, the user leaves), and is the "switch off again" rule independent of how the action ended? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §SC-012]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-001 (switched off whatever way the action ended), research R-06, SC-012.
- [x] CHK021 Is it clear whether a download in progress when Wi-Fi drops can leave anything on the reader outside the store's own area, and does the three-part message say "unchanged"? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-019]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-015 and Edge Cases (nothing is written; message says unchanged), FR-019.

## Home Key, Suspend and Cable

- [x] CHK022 Is the behavior of the reader when the home key is pressed (does the app get an event and time to react, or is it ended at once) stated as a device fact with a manual task, since FR-025 depends on being able to "finish first"? [Assumption, Gap, Spec §FR-025, §Background]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Background table (DS-13, DS-08), Assumptions.
- [x] CHK023 Is a bound given for how long "finish first" after the commit point may take, so the user is not left waiting after pressing the home key? [Measurability, Spec §Edge Cases "home key"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-025 (finishing is only renames and deletions; measured in DS-13, target under 10 s).
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for the reader's automatic switch-off or sleep during a long download or write, including whether the store keeps the reader awake? [Gap, Edge Case]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-025 (the store does not keep the reader awake; auto switch-off is a leave request), Background table (DS-13).
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for connecting the USB cable while an operation is running (the reader may switch to storage mode and unmount the volume)? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §Assumptions "storage is not mounted by a computer while the store runs"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-025 (cable = leave request; an unmounted volume gives E-STO-10; the next start repairs), Background table.
- [x] CHK026 Is the home key during a *repair* covered (the repair must be safe to stop, and the next start repeats it), and the same for a second launch of the store while one is running? [Coverage, Spec §FR-024, §FR-029]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-025 (repair included), FR-029, FR-024 (second launch meets the lock: E-INS-34).

## Recovery of Operations Left by the Installer or the Store

- [x] CHK027 Does the spec say whether the journal records which program wrote it, and does the "which of the two it did" message depend on that, or is it only about finish versus undo? [Clarity, Spec §Story 6 scenario 1, §FR-028]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-028 (the journal does not record the program; 'which of the two' means finish or undo), Story 6.
- [x] CHK028 Is the order of the start-up steps fixed and consistent: launcher swap of a prepared update (FR-033), the interrupted-operation check (FR-028), the repair confirmation, the "start succeeded" mark (FR-034)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028, §FR-033, §FR-034]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-028 (fixed start-up order, four steps).
- [x] CHK029 Is it defined which program performs the recovery of an operation that was interrupted *while swapping the store's own files*, given that the store itself may be half in place and only the launcher can run? [Gap, Spec §FR-036, §Assumptions "launcher"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-030 and FR-036 (engine part by the store's repair; copy and swap by the launcher), launcher contract.
- [x] CHK030 Is the case of a journal or record in a newer format reconciled with the self-update: the message says "the store needs updating", yet the store cannot be updated while it cannot read the catalog or the journal; is the way out (the installer on a computer) stated for this case too? [Consistency, Spec §FR-029, §Edge Cases "newer schema"]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-029 (the message names PB Installer on a computer as the way out).
- [x] CHK031 Is the claim that the installer repairs what the store left (FR-030) backed by a requirement on the installer side, or does it depend on a change to feature 002 that the spec does not name (for example the new `system/pbstore/app/` folder and the self-update state)? [Dependency, Gap, Spec §FR-030, §FR-041]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-030 (no installer change needed: journal and records unchanged; run/ is outside the journal), SC-003; the one installer change is W-INS-04.
- [x] CHK032 Is the install record's version and the version that actually runs defined for the interval between "prepared" and "swapped" (which is recorded, and what does the list show)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-032, §FR-014]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-032 (record names the new version at commit; the list shows the staged note; About shows the running version), research R-12.

## Self-Update: Staging, Swap, Fallback

- [x] CHK033 Is "the new version has started successfully once" decided for the start where the user declines a pending repair or leaves the store at once; does showing the list in the browse-only mode count, and what if the user presses the home key before the list appears? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-034, §FR-035]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-034 and FR-035 (declining the repair counts; leaving with status 0 before the first screen is not a failure).
- [x] CHK034 Is the failure of a start bounded in time (how long may a start take before the next opening counts it as failed), instead of "does not reach its list"? [Measurability, Spec §FR-035, §SC-007]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-035 (a start fails on abnormal end, or the launcher ended before the first screen; no timer, by design), research R-05.
- [x] CHK035 Is it stated what is kept to make the fallback possible when the failing new version also carries a *newer list of trusted keys*, so the old version cannot verify a catalog signed with the next key? [Gap, Spec §FR-035; constitution Principle III key rotation]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-035 (a release trusts the next key before the catalog is signed with it), research R-04, docs/maintainer-keys.md.
- [x] CHK036 After a failed self-update, is it defined whether the catalog still offers that version (the user may try again, or the store marks it as failed), given only that it "MUST NOT be tried again by itself"? [Gap, Spec §FR-035]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-035 (the failed version is not offered again; a newer one is; retry of the same one is the installer's job).
- [x] CHK037 Are requirements stated for a second self-update prepared while one is already prepared, and for the installer on a computer changing or removing the store between "prepared" and "swapped"? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-032, §FR-033]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-032 (a second update replaces the first; installer changes before the swap are compared at the next start).
- [x] CHK038 Does the spec say what is shown, and by which program, when the prepared files fail their hash check at the swap (FR-033), and that this leaves a complete old version and no journal? [Completeness, Spec §FR-033]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-033 (E-STO-07, previous version keeps running, no journal, shown by the store program), store-rules.
- [x] CHK039 Is the state after "started once" but before the old version is deleted covered for a power loss (two complete versions present), and is it defined as a state that story 6 repairs without a user message? [Gap, Spec §FR-034, §FR-036]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-036 (two complete versions is not an error; the launcher removes the old copy silently), launcher S2.
- [x] CHK040 Is it consistent that the swap at the next start writes to the reader without a new confirmation (Principle V: no silent change) while the user confirmed only at "Update"? Is the visible result (the message after the swap) required in every outcome, including fallback? [Consistency, Spec §Story 7 scenarios 2 and 4; constitution Principle V]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec FR-033 (the update confirmation covers the swap; every outcome is shown), FR-032 (plan page line).

## Acceptance Criteria and Traceability

- [x] CHK041 Do the success criteria cover each user-listed hazard with a measurable case: power loss (SC-003), empty battery before a write, Wi-Fi dropping in the middle of a download, the home key in the middle of an install, and free-space exhaustion? [Coverage, Spec §SC-003, §SC-006, §SC-007]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec SC-003, SC-006 (low battery, Wi-Fi lost during a download, full storage, memory), SC-013 (leave at every step), SC-012.
- [x] CHK042 Is SC-003 clear whether the fault test of the *reader* implementation of the file interfaces is the same suite as the installer's fault matrix, as constitution Principle VI requires (same contract tests on the host against a fake reader tree)? [Traceability, Spec §SC-003, §FR-014]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec SC-003 (same suite as feature 002's fault matrix through the store's entry points), quickstart test_store_fault_matrix.
- [x] CHK043 Are the device-only behaviors these requirements rely on (home key, battery reading, flush to the volume, USB connection while running, auto-off, launcher fallback) each listed as "unverified" with a manual device task, as constitution 2.1.0 requires? [Traceability, Spec §Background, §SC-011]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Background table (each device-only behavior with its DS task), research R-17.
- [x] CHK044 Does the spec require that the reader-layout contract (`docs/contracts/reader-layout.md`) and the journal contract be updated for `system/pbstore/app/` before the store writes there, and is that listed as a dependency? [Dependency, Spec §FR-040, §FR-041; constitution Principle VII]
  - Resolved 2026-10-28: spec Assumptions (dependencies: reader-layout line, maintainer-keys rule), quickstart §5.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Most likely to change the spec: CHK011 (battery vs pending repair), CHK013 (space check before the download), CHK029 (who recovers a half-done swap), CHK033 and CHK034 (what "started successfully" means), CHK035 (key rotation vs fallback).
